subject: Acme - Invoice estimate & token volume follow-up
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-20T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: Acme discovery — token volumes & budget

Hi Alex — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and next steps so we’re aligned: 

- Volume profile: you mentioned ~10M inference tokens/day for the search reranking pipeline, plus ~2M tokens/day for support chat (peak). That’s ~360M tokens/month baseline, up to ~500M with growth.
- Target unit economics: you’re shooting for ~$X–$Y per 1M tokens (you said target ~$25/1M tokens as a ballpark).
- Main constraints: predictable monthly spend (finance needs an invoice estimate) and SOC2 evidence for production.

Next steps I’ll take:
1) Share a back-of-envelope invoice estimate and cost model (attached) showing per-1M token unit costs across hosted vs. dedicated options.
2) Loop in Marissa for an SRE/SE review of the latency profile and recommended batching/kv-cache settings.
3) If the numbers look good, we can draft an initial mutual action plan and procurement checklist for your finance team.

Attachments: mutual-action-plan-acme-20261020.pdf (draft), redwood-cost-model-1m-tokens.csv (cost calc)

If you can confirm the daily token split (inference vs embeddings vs chat) and your preferred invoice cadence (monthly vs. quarterly), I’ll update the estimate.

Thanks,
Sean
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-21T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Acme discovery — token volumes & budget

Thanks Sean — appreciate the recap. Couple clarifications: 

- Token split (expected steady-state): 85% inference for reranking (10M/day), 10% chat (2M/day), 5% embeddings for analytics (~600k/day). Peaks could be +30% on marketing days.
- Finance wants an estimate showing: monthly invoice for 1) baseline usage, 2) 20% buffer, 3) overage unit price.
- Target budget: we’re evaluating options to keep platform costs under ~$12k–$15k/month initially. That roughly maps to ~X–Y $/1M tokens—open to your model numbers.

Please send the invoice estimate and a short one-pager we can share with procurement. Procurement contact is procurement@acme.com — loop them when ready.

Alex
Alex Johnson
Senior Product Manager, Search
Acme Corporation

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-22T08:42:00-07:00
Subject: Acme — invoice estimate & cost model (attached)

Hi Alex / Procurement — attaching a conservative invoice estimate and the underlying cost model. Highlights: 

- Baseline monthly tokens (85% rerank + 10% chat + 5% embeddings): ~360M tokens/month. With a 20% buffer that’s ~432M tokens/month.
- Hosted (pay-as-you-go) estimate: list price blended ~ $42.50 per 1M tokens -> baseline invoice ~$15.4k/month; with buffer ~$18.4k/month.
- Dedicated reserved capacity (12-month commit) estimate: effective blended unit cost ~ $22.00 per 1M tokens -> baseline ~$7.9k/month; with buffer ~$9.5k/month.
- Overage / burst: we recommend a hybrid policy (dedicated baseline + hosted burst) to control cost while preserving headroom for spikes.

Attachments included: acme-invoice-estimate-20261022.xlsx (invoice view), redwood-cost-model-1m-tokens.csv (calc). I also added a 1-page summary PDF in the Drive link.

Notes / assumptions are in the first tab of the spreadsheet (avg seq length, tokenization, KV cache hit-rate of 35%, batching improvements). If you want, Marissa can run a quick sensitivity analysis on cache hit-rate and seq length tomorrow.

Next asks: 
- Alex / Procurement: confirm target cadence (monthly) and whether Pricing team needs an NDA copy or a contract redline.
- Alex: confirm if the ~20% buffer is acceptable.

Thanks,
Sean

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-22T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Acme — invoice estimate & cost model (attached)

Hi all — quick follow-up from an SE perspective after glancing at the calc: 

- If Acme can commit to the 12-month reserved capacity we modeled, the per-1M token unit economics look realistic at ~$22/1M tokens. The biggest lever is KV cache hit-rate (going from 35% -> 55% reduces effective tokens by ~18%). I added a sensitivity table in the CSV.
- For procurement: invoice spreadsheet includes line items for Reserved Capacity (monthly commit), Hosted Burst, and an optional Support + SLO add-on. I can extract a single-page procurement-friendly one-pager if you prefer.
- Action: Sean / Alex — if you confirm reserved vs hosted preference I’ll prepare a short statement of work and a draft SOW pricing appendix for legal.

Happy to jump on a 20–30m call tomorrow to walk through the spreadsheet with Procurement.

Best,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
